\textbf{Scope:} text moved on 25 September out of the engine book: engine\_\allowbreak{}table.md (M2, M5, M9, M10, M12 and M14), noise\_\allowbreak{}sieve\_\allowbreak{}tower.md (§14 and §15, and its lines on the program's node policies, links, random numbers, edge rows and floor) and tessera\_\allowbreak{}scheduler.md (the driver's jobs). Each part names where it stood, and its words are as they stood there. Statuses follow \hyperref[chap:readme]{README.md}.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{M5. The correlation operator C}{M5. The correlation operator C}}

The box (\texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}box}, 23 September) on 44b6\_\allowbreak{}0113de3b: \textbf{proved}. C is read at the 27 shifts around every climbed lag and at the drift for 726,273 climbers (every forward pair and every null draw): 20,335,644 cells, 30,196,969 entries, 15.3 s. A cell meeting more labels than the kernel's table (10,507 cells) writes its raw pieces and the host merges them, with no cap. \subsection{\texorpdfstring{M14. The scheduler}{M14. The scheduler}}

\texttt{track\_\allowbreak{}driver} submits through it (24 September): \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}ingest} is one job and each \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}run} part is one; the signum is the part's name and the whole effective request; the declaration is the largest sample's lattice in 16-bit lanes, from the source's description for \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}ingest} (\texttt{engine\_\allowbreak{}source\_\allowbreak{}lanes}, which reads no voxel) and from the \texttt{.\allowbreak{}iapx} head otherwise; the times are 2 s holding, 20 ms sweep and 5 s idle; a job that is not taken, or is held and lost, fails its part. \textbf{Measured} on 44b6\_\allowbreak{}0113de3b, with the driver and the daemon built to \texttt{build/\allowbreak{}verify\_\allowbreak{}driver} (exit 0) and run in a scratch \texttt{TESSERA\_\allowbreak{}STATE}. The ingest was granted its declaration of 838,860,800 bytes and peaked at 5,091,037,184 (25,392 ms), sample root ad3d9846…, set root b68d522c…. Two proves in a row were each granted 838,860,800 and peaked at 3,958,566,912 and 3,962,761,216, with the same roots. The history was then 128 bytes, two records and the seal, and the daemon ended once idle. Anchor\_\allowbreak{}sift's run on the real state gave the same declarations and ingest peak, and the two prove peaks in the other order: identical requests measured 4,194,304 bytes (2\textasciicircum{}22) apart.

\section{\texorpdfstring{From the tessera scheduler: the driver submits (24 September)}{From the tessera scheduler: the driver submits (24 September)}}

\texttt{track\_\allowbreak{}driver} runs every job through tessera. \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}ingest} is one job, and so is each \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}run} part.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The signum} is the BLAKE3 hash of the part's name, a NUL, and the whole effective request, so a changed setting is a new signum.
\item \textbf{The declaration} is the largest sample's lattice in 16-bit lanes. For \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}ingest} it comes from the source's description (\texttt{engine\_\allowbreak{}source\_\allowbreak{}lanes}, which reads no voxel); for every other part, from the \texttt{.\allowbreak{}iapx} head.
\item \textbf{The times} are 2 s holding, 20 ms sweep and 5 s idle.
\item \textbf{The daemon} is \texttt{tessera\_\allowbreak{}daemon} beside the driver, which the driver starts when none answers.
\item \textbf{A part fails} if its job is not taken, or is held and lost; \texttt{-\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}override} admits a held job on its declaration.
\end{itemize}

Measured on 44b6\_\allowbreak{}0113de3b, in a scratch state directory:

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{14. The sieve on this competition: splits, entropy, and each body's harmonics}{14. The sieve on this competition: splits, entropy, and each body's harmonics}}

\texttt{noise\_\allowbreak{}sieve\_\allowbreak{}5\_\allowbreak{}cell\_\allowbreak{}tracking\_\allowbreak{}harmonics.\allowbreak{}pdf} sets the sieve on the Biohub volumes directly. It is the source nearest the score, and each of its mechanics has a concrete form here.

\textbf{The engine holds nothing; gradients define themselves.} No gradient is tuned and no threshold is chosen: the field carves the boundaries where the data puts them. This is already the engine's rule for its cuts. It is also the rule the node policies \texttt{stands} and \texttt{above\_\allowbreak{}null} were written to: a body is a node because of what it is here, not because it ranks in a chosen top n.

\textbf{One precision note.} The source speaks of a 10\textasciicircum{}−68 precision floor. The engine has no precision floor: its arithmetic is exact at every width it runs, and every width is proved before the run. The only floor is the measured one in the data (noise\_\allowbreak{}sieve\_\allowbreak{}tower §5).

\textbf{A split is a boundary discontinuity, judged over the whole sample.} A mitosis or a lysis is not decided in the frame it happens in. Over the sample's whole history there will be a bump in entropy at about that time, and the two differ: a mitosis is a clean fork where local entropy bumps and settles, while a lysis is an uncontained dissipation into the background. Both change the fluidics far around them. The metric pays for this: the division Jaccard is 0.1 of the score, and the engine earns none of it today (0 divisions matched on the older components dump). The test is concrete. A body's fate is already written for every body (\texttt{bodies}: split, merged, vanished, absorbed). The entropy of the region around a candidate split, taken per frame from the exact residual, can say whether a real fork happened. Two linked children and a bump that settles make a division; a bump that bleeds into the floor is a lysis.

\textbf{Each body's harmonics are its second moments.} The source asks for each body's spherical harmonic coefficients, with the dipole (ℓ = 1) and quadrupole (ℓ = 2) dominant for the oblate shapes cells take. Up to ℓ = 2, a body's harmonics carry exactly what its moments carry:

ℓ = 0 & one & the mass & \texttt{MAX\_\allowbreak{}TREE\_\allowbreak{}FIELD\_\allowbreak{}MASS} \\

\end{longtable}
}

So every body the tree finds already carries its ℓ ≤ 2 fingerprint as exact integers, with nothing to fit. The source's “unique harmonics for each body because of intrinsic physical differences” is then a matching rule. A body in the next frame is the same body where its mass, dipole displacement and quadrupole agree, up to the motion the frame shows. The retrograde vector −∇(∂C₁ₘ/∂t) is the time derivative of the dipole: the body's centroid velocity, run backwards to where the motion started.

\textbf{Where it lands on the score.} On the five 6bba samples, 19.6\% of key edges are lost because a cell's link lands on a neighbouring node, a median 6.7 µm from the right one (ledger, 22 September). Neighbouring nodes differ in mass and quadrupole even where their centroids are close, and a body's fingerprint tells it from its neighbours. A link chosen by the ℓ ≤ 2 fingerprint instead of by overlap alone is the direct test of this section.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{15. Edges by jitter, membership by sample coherence}{15. Edges by jitter, membership by sample coherence}}

The engine's rule for what a body is, stated directly: \textbf{the jitter scrubs and oversamples to define a body's edges, and coherence over the whole sample assigns membership.}

\textbf{Edges by jitter.} A single frame's cut puts a boundary voxel on one side or the other by chance: the field noise at the edge decides it. The jitter sweep already in \texttt{relate\_\allowbreak{}frames} (a box a voxel wide, doubling out past the whole view, \texttt{LINK\_\allowbreak{}SWEEP\_\allowbreak{}STEPS}) moves the view by every small offset and asks again. Scrubbing a body's boundary under every jitter oversamples it. The voxels that stay with the body under every offset are its edge; the ones that fall in and out are the floor at its boundary, read and set aside, not averaged. This is noise\_\allowbreak{}sieve\_\allowbreak{}tower §5's floor applied at a body's surface.

\textbf{Membership by sample coherence.} Which pieces make one body is not decided in a frame either. A piece belongs to the body its coherence carries on with across the whole sample, the same way the harmonics source judges a split over the whole sample and not the moment (§14), and the same way identity is the limit of coherence (noise\_\allowbreak{}sieve\_\allowbreak{}tower §9). Pieces of one body cohere through every frame; pieces of two bodies part somewhere in it. So grouping by what touches in one frame, which today runs transitively through touching cells, gives way to grouping by what coheres over all of them.

{\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{6pt}
\begin{longtable}{>{\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}p{\dimexpr0.4140\linewidth-2\tabcolsep\relax}>{\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}p{\dimexpr0.5860\linewidth-2\tabcolsep\relax}}
\toprule
claim & status \\
\midrule
\endhead
the jitter sweep at every offset out to the whole view & built: \texttt{LINK\_\allowbreak{}SWEEP\_\allowbreak{}STEPS}, used today to score a link's disagreement \\
a body's edge is what stays with it under every jitter & theory; the sweep exists, and its use on edges is not built \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
}

\textbf{Never from one frame without context.} Membership is never assigned from a single frame with no knowledge of the local entropy. A frame on its own cannot tell a body's edge from the floor beside it, or two bodies touching from one body. Once there is a history of entropic direction at a place (whether its local entropy is falling toward order, rising toward the floor, or holding), who is what can be derived. A body is where entropy holds low and moves with it. The floor is where entropy sits at its maximum and goes nowhere. A split is a bump that settles into two lows, and a lysis is a bump that rises into the floor.

\textbf{How it is measured, in the engine's terms.} The anchor count already reads every frame of a sample once, per voxel and per bit. The same pass can carry the history at no extra cost. For each bit, it counts the frames whose bit changes from the frame before, the transitions, in windows of frames. A bit at the floor changes about half the time in every window. A bit inside a body barely changes while the body is there. A bit at a moving edge changes in a run, then settles. The windows in time order are the entropic direction at that voxel, as exact integer counts. No logarithm and no float is needed, because the direction is read from how the counts move, not from their size.
